key_insight: An a posteriori framework can directly estimate numerical dissipation in MHD turbulence simulations and shows that it is scale-dependent, anisotropic, and not equivalent to simple effective viscosity/resistivity.
engineering_relevance: This helps simulation practitioners identify when numerical dissipation is contaminating results and choose resolution or physical dissipation settings that better preserve high-fidelity astrophysical MHD turbulence.
method: Estimate numerical dissipation directly from simulation outputs, without a priori assumptions.
Apply the PyMHD framework to Alfvénic turbulence, small-scale dynamos, and MRI-driven turbulence.
Compare spectral and anisotropic properties of numerical dissipation against physical dissipation across regimes.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on multiple MHD turbulence cases, showing that numerical dissipation mainly acts at small scales, inherits turbulence anisotropy, and can be compared against physical dissipation dominance across scales.
watch_item: The inferred dissipation behavior is simulation- and regime-dependent, so it should not be reduced to universal effective coefficients or assumed to behave like physical viscosity/resistivity.
paper_title: Characterization of Numerical Dissipation in Simulations of Magnetohydrodynamic Turbulence
